title: O-Level Combined Science Chemistry: Chemical Reactions and Identification - Worksheet 2
topic: Combustion, Substitution, Addition Reactions, Bromination Tests, and Covalent Bond Calculations
subject: Combined Science Chemistry

questions.question: When a sample of methane gas undergoes complete combustion in a plentiful supply of oxygen gas, what are the only chemical products formed?
options: Carbon monoxide and hydrogen gas
Carbon soot and liquid water
Hydrogen gas and oxygen gas
Carbon dioxide and water vapor
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of any hydrocarbon compound always yields carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water vapor (H₂O) as the final products.

questions.question: A vehicle engine burns a liquid alkane fuel under restricted ventilation conditions, resulting in incomplete combustion. What toxic product is associated with this reaction?
options: Toxic carbon monoxide gas
Pure oxygen gas
Solid calcium carbonate
Pungent sulfur dioxide gas
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion occurs when there is a limited supply of oxygen, producing highly toxic carbon monoxide gas (CO) instead of carbon dioxide.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of performing a bromination test using aqueous bromine on an unknown hydrocarbon sample?
options: To determine the exact number of hydrogen atoms in the sample
To distinguish between a saturated hydrocarbon and an unsaturated hydrocarbon
To increase the boiling point of the hydrocarbon sample
To test if the compound can conduct electricity
questions.explanation: The bromination test is a standard diagnostic test used to distinguish between saturated compounds (alkanes) and unsaturated compounds (alkenes).

questions.question: A student adds reddish-brown bromine water to ethene gas at room temperature in a completely dark room. What is the expected visual observation?
options: The solution remains reddish-brown indefinitely
The solution changes to a deep blue color
A dense black solid precipitate settles at the bottom
The reddish-brown solution decolourises immediately
questions.explanation: Alkenes possess a reactive double bond that undergoes rapid addition reactions with bromine water instantly, requiring no light energy to break the bond.

questions.question: If a few drops of aqueous bromine are mixed with liquid ethane in a test tube kept completely away from light, what will be observed?
options: The reddish-brown colour of bromine decolourises instantly
The mixture begins to boil violently
The reddish-brown colour of bromine remains unchanged
The liquid separates into two brightly colored layers
questions.explanation: Ethane is a saturated alkane. Alkanes do not undergo rapid addition reactions with bromine water and require ultraviolet light or sunlight to undergo substitution, so the reddish-brown color remains unchanged in the dark.

questions.question: Under what specific condition can a saturated alkane like methane react with a halogen like chlorine or bromine?
options: In the presence of ultraviolet light or strong sunlight
Mixed with a solid nickel catalyst at low temperatures
Dissolved in a large volume of an alkaline solution
Alkanes can never react with bromine under any condition
questions.explanation: Alkanes are generally unreactive because they are saturated. They can only undergo a slow substitution reaction with halogens if ultraviolet light is present to provide activation energy.

questions.question: When propene gas is heated to one hundred and fifty degrees Celsius with hydrogen gas over a nickel catalyst, what compound is produced?
options: Ethanol
Propene oxide
Propane
Butane
questions.explanation: This reaction is hydrogenation, an addition reaction where hydrogen atoms add across the double bond of the unsaturated alkene (propene), converting it into the corresponding saturated alkane (propane).

questions.question: What catalyst and temperature conditions are required to carry out the industrial hydrogenation of alkenes?
options: A yeast catalyst at a room temperature of thirty-seven degrees
A nickel catalyst at a temperature of one hundred and fifty degrees
A concentrated acid catalyst at zero degrees
No catalyst is required because the reaction occurs spontaneously
questions.explanation: The addition of hydrogen to an alkene requires a finely divided nickel catalyst and an operating temperature of about one hundred and fifty degrees Celsius.

questions.question: From a conceptual standpoint, what structural transformation occurs during the hydrogenation of an alkene?
options: An unsaturated hydrocarbon is converted into a saturated hydrocarbon
An organic acid is neutralised to form a salt and water
A small polymer molecule is broken down into simple gas monomers
A single covalent bond is converted into a reactive double bond
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation adds hydrogen atoms across a carbon to carbon double bond. This opens up the double bond into single bonds, converting an unsaturated alkene into a saturated alkane.

questions.question: What type of chemical reaction occurs when ethene reacts with bromine water to form dibromoethane?
options: Substitution reaction
Combustion reaction
Decomposition reaction
Addition reaction
questions.explanation: Alkenes undergo addition reactions where the carbon to carbon double bond opens up, allowing atoms to add to the molecule without eliminating any other atoms.

questions.question: What type of reaction takes place when methane gas reacts with chlorine gas in the presence of sunlight?
options: Addition reaction
Substitution reaction
Neutralisation reaction
Thermal cracking
questions.explanation: Alkanes react via substitution reactions, where a hydrogen atom in the alkane molecule is replaced or substituted by a halogen atom.

questions.question: Two fuel samples, propane (an alkane) and propene (an alkene), both contain exactly three carbon atoms per molecule. When burned completely in air, why does propene produce a noticeably sootier flame than propane?
options: Propene has a higher percentage of carbon by mass, leading to more incomplete combustion
Propane contains more carbon atoms per molecule than propene
Propene chemically blocks oxygen from entering the flame zone
Propane undergoes an addition reaction with atmospheric nitrogen
questions.explanation: Propene (C₃H₆) has a lower hydrogen count than propane (C₃H₈), which gives it a higher percentage of carbon by mass. A higher carbon content leads to more incomplete combustion and a sootier flame.

questions.question: A sample containing 20 cm³ of ethene gas undergoes complete hydrogenation to form ethane. What volume of hydrogen gas is completely consumed in this reaction?
options: 10 cm³
40 cm³
20 cm³
60 cm³
questions.explanation: Ethene reacts with hydrogen gas in a one to one mole ratio: C₂H₄ + H₂ → C₂H₆. According to Avogadro's Law, gas volume ratios are equal to mole ratios. Therefore, 20 cm³ of ethene will react with exactly 20 cm³ of hydrogen gas.

questions.question: When a mixture of ethane gas and chlorine gas is exposed to ultraviolet light, a substitution reaction occurs. Alongside the chloroethane organic product, what other chemical product is formed, and what is its observation when tested with moist blue litmus paper?
options: Water vapour which dries the paper
Hydrogen gas which pops with a splint
Oxygen gas which relights a splint
Hydrogen chloride gas which turns it red
questions.explanation: In an alkane substitution reaction, a halogen atom replaces a hydrogen atom, which then links with the remaining halogen atom to form a hydrogen halide gas (HCl). Hydrogen chloride is an acidic gas that dissolves in the moisture of blue litmus paper, turning it red.

questions.question: An unbranched alkane molecule has a relative molecular mass that corresponds to a chain containing exactly 8 carbon atoms (octane). Calculate the total number of single covalent bonds present between all the atoms in this single molecule.
options: Eighteen
Twenty-four
Twenty-five
Twenty-six
questions.explanation: Octane has the formula C₈H₁₈. It contains 7 carbon-to-carbon single bonds and 18 carbon-to-hydrogen single bonds. The total number of single covalent bonds is 7 plus 18, which equals 25.
